takeaway: An adenoma is a slow-growing benign tumour that is typically encapsulated, with a pseudocapsule of compressed tissue.

question.text: Which is a feature of an adenoma?
question.say: Which is a feature of an adenoma?

lines.text: A benign adenoma, resting on its cushion.
lines.say: Here is a calm adenoma, a benign tumour, resting on its red cushion.
It sits inside a clear bubble. Adenomas are typically encapsulated.

lines.text: Slow growth squashes the tissue around it.
lines.say: (sigh) Look at the squashed cells below. As it grows slowly, it compresses the normal tissue around it.
That compressed tissue forms a pseudocapsule.

lines.text: Some cells may be dysplastic, but cannot invade.
lines.say: Some cells may be dysplastic, but they cannot invade the basement membrane or metastasize, so it is still benign.

lines.text: Severe dysplasia equals carcinoma in situ.
lines.say: Dysplasia is a step toward malignancy, and severe dysplasia is the same as carcinoma in situ.

lines.text: Remember: an adenoma is a slow, benign tumour, typically encapsulated.
lines.say: Remember: an adenoma is a slow-growing, benign tumour, typically encapsulated.
